_comment: The corpus the mock search backend ranks over (scripts/life-scenarios/mock-search.mjs).
Every `url` here is a REAL, live page. That is deliberate: the benchmark mocks
*discovery*, not retrieval. The agent still fetches each page over the network with
web_fetch and still has to read what it actually says, so `cites_delta_com` and the
content checks stay honest — what the mock removes is the search engine the run has
no credentials for, not the reading comprehension the scenario is testing.
`excerpts` are snippets in the shape the Parallel/Exa proxy returns. They are hints
for ranking and selection, never a substitute for the page: they deliberately stop
short of the exact numbers the graders assert on, so an agent that answers from the
excerpt alone still fails the check.

documents.title: Carry-On Baggage | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Delta allows one carry-on bag plus one personal item free of charge on every fare, including Basic Economy. The page states the exact maximum dimensions and the linear-inch limit.

documents.title: Baggage Information Overview | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Entry point for Delta's baggage rules: carry-on, checked allowances, size and weight maximums, and the fee structure by cabin and route.

documents.title: Excess & Overweight Baggage Fees | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Per-piece weight and size limits by cabin, and the published excess, overweight and oversized charges for travel between North America and Europe.

documents.title: Previous Baggage Fees | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Historical record of fee changes, including first-bag pricing for Delta Main Basic on U.S./Canada/Mexico to Europe itineraries ticketed before a stated date. A change notice, not the current published fare.

documents.title: Baggage on Partner Airlines | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Which carrier's baggage rules govern an itinerary operated by a partner, which matters on transatlantic routes that Delta codeshares.

documents.title: Special Items & Sports Equipment | Delta Air Lines
excerpts: Handling and charges for items that fall outside the standard checked allowance.

documents.title: Telework and Remote Work — U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
excerpts: Official U.S. federal survey estimates of the share of employed people who teleworked, broken out by industry and occupation. The release carries the reference period the figure belongs to.

documents.title: Telework — U.S. Census Bureau
excerpts: Census Bureau tables tracking work-from-home rates over time, with the year each estimate covers stated alongside it.

documents.title: How Americans View Their Jobs — Remote Work | Pew Research Center
excerpts: Survey of U.S. workers whose jobs can be done from home, reporting how many do so all of the time versus some of the time. Note the fieldwork date when judging whether this is current.
